summary: GDPR documentary artifacts (ROPA/DPIA/DPA) over the security base — Regulation (EU) 2016/679 Arts. 28/30/35. Paperwork existence/metadata/freshness only, never legal adequacy.

namespaces.name: ROPA
namespaces.comment: Records of processing activities (GDPR Art. 30). Each record declares the controller/processor role, an Art. 6(1) lawful basis from the closed vocabulary, the data categories processed, and a retention period — the highest-value defects a ROPA can catch are an undeclared role or an absent/mistyped lawful basis. Path-claim, but carries an `id` (core.id) so DPIAs and DPAs resolve as cross-ref targets. gdpr.processor-dpa (GDPR-002) adds the conditional cross-ref: a processor-role record must link its governing DPA (the Art. 28 agreement).

namespaces.name: DPIA
namespaces.comment: Data protection impact assessments (GDPR Art. 35). A DPIA assesses high-risk processing and must be re-reviewed when that processing changes; `reviewed_date` under core.calendar-freshness flags one stale past a year. Cross-refs the ROPA activity it assesses.

namespaces.name: DPA
namespaces.comment: Processor / subprocessor agreement register (GDPR Art. 28). Each entry records the contracting party and the execution date, making the processing relationship auditable. Path-claim with an `id` so a processor-role ROPA can cross-ref its governing DPA.
